summary: Red team of the extraction of Nelson–Venkatesh, 'The orbit method and analysis of automorphic forms' (Acta Math. 226 (2021) 1–209). It was read in full against the published PDF (hash matches) and arXiv v3, with every finding verified personally. There are fourteen findings: two high, ten medium and two low. The coverage and locators are sound: every numbered statement has an item, all 99 locators are right, the nine library citations hold at the pins, and E1–E15 are confirmed. High: (1) E1 is understated. For (SO3, SO2) with Π dihedral for the torus's field, Theorem 27.1 and the main average (31.3) are false, not just unproven. Multiplication by χ = η_{K/F}∘θ preserves Π, is trivial on H(A) and acts by sign(n) on weight-n vectors at q, so the H-periods vanish for one sign of the archimedean weight. The weak subconvex bound survives. (2) Items /48 and /56 drop 'k algebraically closed' and 'O_{π,σ} ≠ ∅' and are false as written over R. Medium: four items copy false statements (Cotlar–Stein norm convergence, (8.3), Op/Op_h, a sign); other items omit hypotheses. Ownership problems: the real Plancherel theorem and Langlands classification are also routed by BEUZARTPLESSIS-LIU-ZHANG-ETAL-21 (and AF.1b). The p-adic tempered classification is already at SR.3 via GAN-SAVIN-23. GIT/Hilbert–Mumford duplicates FINTZEN-21's accepted Part II. The local relative character is split between the two new roadmaps while the GGP roadmap owns the Ichino–Ikeda integral. Two planned statuses are too generous: Ratner at GN.4, and Chevalley/Harish-Chandra for reductive g at LieHighestWeight layer 7. Cited inputs have no item (local multiplicity one, Schwartz kernel theorem, spinor norm, which Tau Ceti has, compactness criterion, Borel density, Nelson's and Rao's theorems). Sixteen further source mistakes were missed, among them a reversed integration region on p. 136, an incomplete Θ^unit behind E3, and a misattributed [Z1]. Low: the list of GGP proposers is wrong, and sourceVersions and review verdicts are missing.

Disclosure. This session wrote FIX-RT-AREA-automorphic-1 (PR #4648), which proposed AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups:AF.1b (Casselman embedding, Langlands classification, discrete series) and AF.1c (Paley–Wiener). Finding 5 names AF.1b as the owner of the real Langlands classification; its evidence is the merged fixes file and the accepted route of PAPER-BEUZARTPLESSIS-LIU-ZHANG-ETAL-21, not a judgement of mine. This session also wrote PAPER-LUST-STEVENS-20 (which joined SmoothRepresentationsPartII); no finding depends on it. Finding 6 concerns the base roadmap's SR.3, not that Part II.

Crossref has no update or erratum for 10.4310/ACTA.2021.v226.n1.a1 (no 'updated-by', and filter updates: returns 0). A web search found no erratum.

The whole paper was read in a pdftotext extraction with journal page markers, by part: §1 and Parts I–II with Appendix A; Part III (§§13–19, to p. 136); Part IV (§§20–24); Part V (§§25–31). Page images were rendered for pp. 28, 49, 60, 62, 69, 95, 110, 118, 119, 122, 126, 128–131, 133, 134, 136, 165, 182, 185, 191 and 202 to settle symbols. Every finding filed here was verified personally at its locator.

Coverage. Every numbered Definition, Lemma, Proposition, Theorem, Corollary and Conjecture from Lemma 2.1 to Theorem 31.11, and Appendix A's Lemmas A.1–A.4, was listed (about 150 statements) and matched to an item's locator or note. None is missing. The uncovered numbered Examples and Remarks (1.2–1.5, 3.2, 4.2, 4.4, 4.6, 6.2, 7.5, 10.2, 11.7) carry no mathematics used later. §21 (compact H) is covered by /66. The unnumbered cited inputs were enumerated per part; the ones used in proofs without an item are finding 11.
Locators: all 99 item locators (section, number, page) are correct, confirming the review's 88 checks and extending them to all items.

Statements and hypotheses: the main theorems' items against the paper. These are Theorems 4.5, 5.6, 5.8, 6.1, 6.3, 7.4, 8.11, 11.1, 12.2, 14.2, 14.5, 16.7, 17.1–17.2, 19.3, 22.2, 24.5, 26.4, 26.5, 27.1, 27.7, 29.1, 30.1 and 31.11, Lemmas 9.4, 11.6, 15.2–15.4, 18.1, 19.1, 19.5, 23.2–23.4, 24.1, 27.3, 27.12, 31.9 and 31.10, Corollary 31.8, Definition 24.3 and §25.7. The discrepancies are findings 2–4; the rest match, including δ ranges, temperedness and h-dependence.

§25.7 and Theorem 31.11: the pairs allowed ((U_{n+1}, U_n), n ≥ 1; (SO_{n+1}, SO_n), n ≥ 2), anisotropy, G quasi-split and Π generic at q, G_p compact at the other archimedean places. τ(G) = τ(H) = 2 holds for every allowed pair: τ(U_n) = 2, τ(SO_n) = 2 for n ≥ 3, and τ = 2 for the anisotropic norm-one tori (Ono). (1.4) is unconditional as a bound for L(Π, Σ) and follows from (31.1) with Lemma 31.10.

Recorded source issues: E1–E15 checked at their locators. All quotations are exact. E1: verified (spinor norm image N(K_v^×)F_v^{×2} for SO2; χ = η∘θ kills G(F)H(A)G(A)^+ and U for small U) and strengthened (finding 1). E2: confirmed; the phase in Lemma 7.7 is not affine, so ∆φ ≠ 0. findings.claim: E1 understates the problem. The extraction records only that the proof of Lemma 27.3 fails for (G, H) = (SO3, SO2) and leaves open (gap G-SO3, status 'open') whether Theorem 27.1 and Theorem 31.11 actually fail when Π ≅ Π ⊗ (η_{K/F}∘θ). They do fail. Take Π dihedral with respect to K = F(√−disc V_H), so that the automorphic character χ := η_{K/F}∘θ of G(A) satisfies Π ⊗ χ ≅ Π. Then the H-period of Π against Σ vanishes identically for every Σ whose archimedean weight at q has one sign (for K_q = C), so for a one-sided admissible U the average (31.3) of L(Π, Σ) over F_h tends to 0, not to 1/τ(G) = 1/2; and (27.1) fails for suitable a. The weak subconvex bound (1.4) survives, with the loss of a factor at most 2. The same sentence of the proof also claims local surjectivity of the spinor norm on SO_{n−1} at every place, which is false at real places where V_H is definite even when n − 1 ≥ 3; there the conclusion is recovered globally (Kneser), so only the proof is affected.
findings.evidence: Paper: Acta Math. 226 (2021), p. 181, Theorem 27.1: 'For any a∈S(g∧), (1/τ(H))∫_{[H]}[a] = (1/τ(G))∫_{[G]}[a].' p. 182, proof of Lemma 27.3: 'G=SO_n: in this case, the spinor norm injects G(F_v)/G(F_v)^+ into F_v^× modulo squares, and our assertion follows from the surjectivity of the spinor norm on SO_{n−1} (for n−1⩾2).' §25.7 (p. 171) allows '(SO_{n+1}, SO_n) with n⩾2' with G anisotropic, G_q quasi-split and Π tempered and generic at q; Theorem 31.11 (pp. 203–204) asserts (1/|F_h|)Σ_{Σ∈F_h} L(Π, Σ) = 1/τ(G) + o(1) for every admissible U, U′. Argument (checked by this red team). (i) Data: F = Q, D a quaternion division algebra over Q split at ∞, G = PD^× = SO(D^0, Nrd) (anisotropic, G_∞ = PGL2(R) quasi-split), K ⊂ D an imaginary quadratic field, H = K^×/Q^× = SO(V_H) with V_H = K^⊥ ∩ D^0, Π the Jacquet–Langlands transfer of a dihedral π(ψ), ψ a Hecke character of K, with discrete series at the places where D ramifies; Π is tempered, a discrete series D_k (k ≥ 2) at q = ∞, and Π ⊗ (η_K∘Nrd) ≅ Π. On PD^× the spinor norm is Nrd modulo squares, so χ = η_K∘Nrd. (ii) χ is trivial on G(F) (reciprocity), on H(A) (θ(H(A)) consists of norms from A_K^×) and on G(A)^+. Hence for every φ in Π and every character Σ of [H], ∫_{[H]}φΣ̄ = ∫_{[H]}(χφ)Σ̄. (iii) Multiplication by χ preserves Π (multiplicity one for D^×) and factors as ⊗_v M_v with M_v : π_v → π_v ⊗ χ_v. At q, χ_q = sgn∘det (η_{C/R} = sign, θ = det mod squares); M_q commutes with PGL2(R)^+, which contains H_q = SO(2), and anticommutes with elements of negative determinant, which swap the holomorphic and antiholomorphic halves D^± of D_k; so M_q = c on D^+ and −c on D^−, i.e. it acts on a vector of SO(2)-weight n by c·sgn(n). At v ≠ q, χ_v is trivial on H(F_v), so ℓ∘M_v = c_v(σ′_v)ℓ for the unique (Tunnell–Saito multiplicity one) H(F_v)-functional ℓ, with c_v = ±1. (iv) Therefore the Σ-period of φ_n ⊗ φ′ equals c·sgn(n)·∏_v c_v(σ′_v) times itself, and vanishes identically on the Σ-isotypic part whenever that sign is −1. For fixed σ′ this happens for all Σ whose weight n at q has one fixed sign; for those Σ the branching coefficient L(Π, Σ) of §25.4 is 0. Taking the finite places of R non-split in K (so H(F_v) = K_v^×/F_v^× is compact there and singletons are allowable, §21) and U′ = {σ′} and U a compact interval of that sign in [h^∧] = R ∖ {0} (all of which is stable, the limit orbit of D_k being the nilcone), F_h is non-empty and every term of (31.3) is 0, so the average tends to 0 ≠ 1/2. This is the ε-dichotomy phenomenon for CM forms: L(½, π_K ⊗ Ω) = L(½, ψΩ)L(½, ψ^cΩ), and one factor has root number −1 for one sign of the weight. (v) In the language of the proof: [a] is a function on the finite group ε = G(F)G∞^+U\G(A); the image of H(A) is the kernel of χ (index 2), so ∫_{[H]}[a] = τ(H)(c_1 + c_χ) while ∫_{[G]}[a] = τ(G)c_1, and (27.1) holds iff ∫_{[G]}[a]χ = 0; for a supported on the half-cone O^+ this integral is a non-zero multiple of ∫_{O^+}a·⟨M′u, u⟩. (vi) (1.4) survives: [a] ≥ 0 (Theorem 26.4(iv)) and the image of H(A) has index ≤ 2 in ε, so (1/τ(H))∫_{[H]}[a] ≤ 2(1/τ(G))∫_{[G]}[a], and the upper bound (31.1) with Lemma 31.10 still gives L(Π, Σ) = o(C^{1/4}). (vii) Real places: at a real place where V_H is definite and V is not, θ(SO(V_H)(R)) is trivial while θ(SO(V)(R)) = {±1}, so the place-by-place argument fails for every n; for dim V_H ≥ 3 Kneser's theorem θ(G(F)) = F^× ∩ θ(G(A)) supplies the missing sign from G(F). The unitary case is unaffected (det : U(V_H) → U_1 is onto). Both texts: identical in arXiv v3 (proof of Lemma 27.3).

findings.claim: Two item statements drop a hypothesis and are false as written. /48 states Theorem 14.5 without 'k algebraically closed': 'each fibre O^{λ,µ} is an H-torsor. The map g → [g]×[h] is surjective'. Over R both fail. /56 states '(17.3) O_{π,σ} = O_π(λ_σ) = O^{λ_π,λ_σ} when stable' without the paper's 'and O_{π,σ} is non-empty'; over R O_{π,σ} can be empty while O_π(λ_σ) is not.
findings.evidence: p. 99, §14.3: 'We retain the setting of §14.2, and assume that k is algebraically closed. Theorem 14.5. The morphism of varieties {H-stable x∈g} → {stable (λ, µ)∈[g]×[h]} …'. p. 117: 'Theorem 17.1 implies that if (λ_π, λ_σ) is stable and O_{π,σ} is non-empty, then O_{π,σ} is an H-torsor consisting of H-stable elements, and hence O_{π,σ} = O_π(λ_σ) = O^{λ_π,λ_σ} (17.3)'; Theorem 17.1 itself says 'either O^{λ,µ}=∅, or O^{λ,µ} is an H-torsor'. Counterexample to /48 over R: (G, H) = (SO(3), SO(2)); for x ∈ so(3), ev(x) = {±ia} with a = |x|, and ev(x_H) = {±ib} with |b| ≤ a; a pair (a, b) with |b| > a is stable (disjoint eigenvalues) but not in the image, so its fibre is empty and g → [g]×[h] is not surjective. For /56: for SO(2,1) two real orbits share an infinitesimal character, so O_σ may be a proper part of the fibre over λ_σ.

Item /56: replace 'when stable' by 'when (λ_π, λ_σ) is stable and O_{π,σ} is non-empty'.

findings.claim: Four items copy false or mis-signed statements from the paper, and none of these mistakes is in sourceIssues. /26 states Cotlar–Stein with 'Σ_j T_j converges in operator norm', which is false; the series converges strongly. /23 copies (8.3), which is false for α ≠ 0 (a factor h^{−|α|} is missing). /3 copies the rescaled composition formula with Op where Op_h is meant. /22 copies the sign (−h)^j of Lemma 7.14, which under the paper's own convention (4.1) is h^j.
findings.evidence: p. 61–62, Lemma 8.10: 'Then, the series T := Σ_j T_j converges in the Banach space of bounded linear operators from V1 to V2, and has operator norm ‖T‖⩽C.' Counterexample: T_j the orthogonal projection onto Ce_j for an orthonormal sequence; T_j^*T_k = T_jT_k^* = δ_{jk}T_j, so both Cotlar–Stein sums are 1, but the partial sums are projections with ‖S_n − S_m‖ = 1. p. 57, Lemma 8.1(ii): 'More generally, for a∈S^m_δ, ∂^α a_h^∨(x) ≪ h^{−dim(g)} |x/h^{1−δ}|^{−N}. (8.3)'. Since a_h^∨(x) = h^{−n}a^∨(x/h), ∂^α a_h^∨(x) = h^{−n−|α|}(∂^α a^∨)(x/h); for a fixed Schwartz a, δ = 0, α = e_1 and |x| = h the left side is ≍ h^{−n−1} and the right side ≍ h^{−n}. p. 28, §2.5: 'Op_h(a, χ)Op_h(b, χ) = Op(a⋆_h b, χ′), where … (a⋆_h b)_h = a_h⋆b_h' — then Op_h(a)Op_h(b) = Op(a_h⋆b_h) = Op((a⋆_h b)_h) = Op_h(a⋆_h b); Theorem 5.8 (p. 40) writes Op_h. p. 56, Lemma 7.14: 'b ≡ Σ_{0⩽j<J}(−h)^j Σ_{|α|=j}(∂^αψ(0)/α!)∂^αa'; with (4.1) '(∂^αa)^∨(x) = x^αa^∨(x)', b_h^∨ = ψa_h^∨ = Σ(∂^αψ(0)/α!)x^αa_h^∨ = Σ(∂^αψ(0)/α!)(∂^α a_h)^∨ and ∂^α(a_h) = h^{|α|}(∂^αa)_h, so the sign is +. All four texts are identical in arXiv v3. None affects a downstream result (Proposition 8.7 needs only strong convergence and the norm bound; (8.3) is used where N is arbitrary).

findings.claim: Route 1 makes the new orbit-method roadmap plan Harish-Chandra's Plancherel formula and the Langlands classification for real reductive groups. Both are already planned by another accepted route, and the classification also by an accepted fix. findings.claim: The status is wrong: GN.4 does not plan Ratner's measure classification in the generality the paper uses. The paper needs it for an arbitrary semisimple real Lie group G∞ with an arithmetic lattice Γ and the subgroup generated by the unipotent part of a regular nilpotent centralizer, together with the ergodic decomposition. GN.4 schedules only 'unipotent-flow … proofs needed for Oppenheim/Duke-type arithmetic applications'. Its blueprint has no Ratner node, and its remaining work lists only 'independent mixing/nondivergence/Oppenheim/Duke branches'. The extraction itself says a reviewer 'may prefer to route Ratner separately', and nothing does. Borel's density theorem, used in the same proof (Lemma 27.8), has no item at all.

findings.claim: Several cited or standard theorems that the proofs depend on have no item, contrary to the stated coverage policy ('cited theorems the proofs depend on … are items'). (a) Local multiplicity one, dim Hom_H(π, σ) ≤ 1 (Sun–Zhu; Aizenbud–Gourevitch–Rallis–Schiffmann). It is used to define ℓ_σ (Remark 18.2, §20) and the branching coefficient, is listed only as a prerequisite, and is owned by the GGP roadmap through PAPER-JIANG-ZHANG-20 'bessel-uniqueness'. (b) The Schwartz kernel theorem, used to build the measure η in Theorem 26.5; it is in neither library. (c) The Riesz–Markov–Kakutani theorem, used in the same proof; it is in Mathlib. (d) The spinor norm, and the description of G(F_v)/G(F_v)^+ by it and by det, which is the locus of E1; Tau Ceti has the spinor norm with Spin image = kernel. (e) The compactness criterion for anisotropic groups, used in Lemma 27.8 and §25.7, which AdelicAlgebraicGroups:AA.3 plans. (f) Nelson's theorems that ∆ is essentially self-adjoint and positive with π^∞ = ∩D(∆^n), which underlie every Sobolev statement of Part I. (g) Rao's theorem that orbital measures are locally finite. (h) Uniform admissibility, dim σ^J bounded over Ĥ, used in Step 6 of §24.4. (i) Cartan's theorem that G^sc(F_q) is connected, used in Lemma 27.11.

findings.claim: The extraction missed further mistakes in the paper, and two recorded ones need correcting. Each of the following was checked at the published locator and is also in arXiv v3 unless noted. (i) p. 136, §19.8: the integration region is reversed; it should be ‖s−1‖ ⩽ h^{1/2−η}, since Lemma 19.8 makes exactly the printed region O(h^∞). (ii) p. 147, (22.10): the proof chooses a with |k − ∫_{O(µ)}a²| ≤ ε₁ on all of U but a₂ only large on U₀, so the exact inequality is not proved outside U₀; the proof gives (22.10) with an added O(h^N), which suffices for Theorem 30.1. (iii) p. 165, Example 24.7: Θ^unit and Θ^nt omit the negative real interval (α = −q^{±s}, 0 ≤ s ≤ ½: η∘det, St ⊗ η∘det, the twisted complementary series). So E3's correction, which repeats 'Θ^unit ≅ C^(1) ∪ [q^{−1/2}, q^{1/2}]', is incomplete, and for odd n the example also fails f ≥ 1 on the negative part of Θ^nt. (iv) p. 185, Lemma 27.10: 'This implies s⩽g' should be s ⩾ g. (v) p. 4: 'the size of the family F_h is roughly the fourth power of the analytic conductor' is reversed (C ≍ |F_h|⁴, Lemma 31.10). (vi) p. 136, §A.1: κ = −cΣx² acts by 0 on the trivial K-type, contradicting (ii) dim τ ⩽ κ_τ^{1/2} and Lemma A.1(ii). (vii) p. 110, §16.5: O^{λ,µ} is called the fibre of g*×h* → [g*]×[h*], which is O^λ×O^µ of dimension 2 dim H; the map is g* → [g*]×[h*]. (viii) p. 95, proof of Lemma 13.2: the dim(U′) = 1 line of the centralizer list omits y (published text only; arXiv v3 has it). (ix) p. 134, proof of Lemma 19.8: 'ψ≡1 on B(ω, 2h^δ), and ψ≡0 on B(ω, 3h^δ)' should read 'outside B(ω, 3h^δ)'. (x) p. 79, proof of Lemma 10.1: b₂ = −(q⋆²b₀ + q⋆¹b₁)/q, not (−q⋆²b₀ + q⋆¹b₁)/q. (xi) p. 69, §8.8.6: the right-division recursion should be q₁ = −(q₀⋆¹Z)/Z with Z = z^{s+2k}, not −(b⋆¹q₀)/Z. (xii) p. 43: d is half the maximal orbit dimension. (xiii) p. 88, (12.3): '(O, π)' for (O, ω). (xiv) p. 191: '|tr(T1T2)|² ⩽ tr(T1∗T2)tr(T2∗T2)' should have tr(T1∗T1). (xv) pp. 3 and 203–204: [Z1] (Zhang, Ann. of Math. 180) proves the global GGP conjecture, not the Ichino–Ikeda/N. Harris formula (1.1); the refinement is Zhang's subsequent paper. [Z1]'s hypotheses (every archimedean place split in E/F) together with §25.7(3) and anisotropy leave only (U2, U1). The extraction's /81 note repeats the claim. (xvi) E15's locator 'p. 154 (Lemmas 23.3–23.4)': Lemma 23.4 is on p. 155, and the same G-for-H slips recur in §23.1 and the proof of Lemma 23.2.
